(2) Caused perfection is received in the effect: caused by another implies participated, participated implies received in the participant. (3) The cause's perfection is not received in its effect: a haver depends on its recipient, perfection-causing in another is efficient (explicit DISAMB-CAUSE bridge), and target (4). (4) An efficient cause does not depend on its effect: the stated q.2 a.3 no-self-causation, q.44 a.1 ad 2 dependence, and asymmetry of dependence among distinct beings. (5) Nonmutual dependence suffices for priority: the criterion 'can be without, not conversely' (In V Metaph. lect. 13 n. 15, navigation only) with two bridges between counterfactual dependence and being-without. (6) Others than the primary are creatures: q.44 a.1 participated esse of everything else, the existing q.44 a.1 ad 1 statement, and caused-in-being implies creature. (7) Strict primacy: target (6), creature esse received, both q.7 directions (received esse limited; limited only through reception), the primary's esse unreceived, and limited esse approaches less. (8) Universal cause transfers perfections: universal cause of being is total, total cause causes modes of being, perfections are modes of being (q.4 a.2).
